proposals.rule: You can come to the UK for a maximum of up to 12 months, or the time given in your certificate of sponsorship plus up to 28 days, whichever is shorter.
proposals.exception: changes in this guidance will permit seasonal workers to spend no more than 6 months working in the UK during any rolling 10-month period, rather than any rolling 12-month period
proposals.why: the exception narrows the stay limit for seasonal workers to 6 months in a rolling 10‑month window

proposals.rule: You can stay in the UK for up to 14 days after the date your job ends, as long as you do not stay past the end date on your visa.
proposals.exception: changes in this guidance will permit seasonal workers to spend no more than 6 months working in the UK during any rolling 10-month period, rather than any rolling 12-month period
proposals.why: exception narrows the stay period for seasonal workers to a maximum of 6 months in any rolling 10‑month window, reducing the general 14‑day post‑job stay rule

proposals.rule: You can stay in the UK: up to 6 months for horticulture work
proposals.exception: changes in this guidance will permit seasonal workers to spend no more than 6 months working in the UK during any rolling 10-month period, rather than any rolling 12-month period
proposals.why: the exception narrows the duration rule by adding a rolling‑10‑month limit for all seasonal workers

proposals.rule: The applicant must have met the continuous residence requirement set out in Appendix Continuous Residence for the entirety of the qualifying period.
proposals.exception: For any absence from the UK with permission granted under the rules in place before 11 January 2018, the applicant must not have been outside the UK for more than 180 days during any consecutive 12‑month period, ending on the same date of their current application unless CR 3.3 applies, and subject to CR 3.4.
proposals.why: The exception narrows the continuous residence requirement to a 180‑day limit for absences under pre‑2018 permissions, changing the outcome for that specific case.

proposals.rule: If you’re 18 or over, you can only apply if you have permission to stay in the UK (‘leave to enter or remain’) which started when you were under 18.
proposals.exception: The applicant may be aged 18 or older on the date of application if the applicant was last granted entry clearance or permission to stay as the dependent child of their parent or parents, and either: (a) the entry clearance or permission to stay is valid on the date of application or expired no more than 14 days before the date of application, except that where the Exceptions for overstayers section of Part Suitability applies that period of overstaying will be disregarded; or (b) the applicant is applying as a dependent child under Appendix Bereaved Partner or Appendix Victim of Domestic Abuse.
proposals.why: covers 18+ applicants who were previously granted entry clearance as a dependent child, allowing them to apply despite the general rule.

proposals.rule: You can stay in the UK for 2 years and 9 months on this visa. After this you’ll need to apply to extend your stay.
proposals.exception: If you extend your family visa or switch to this visa you can stay in the UK for 2 years and 6 months.
proposals.why: The exception narrows the stay period to 2 years 6 months for those extending or switching visas, differing from the general 2 years 9 months rule.

proposals.rule: CHI 1.1. The applicant must be under the age of 18 on the date of application unless CHI 1.2 applies.
proposals.exception: Where a child has reached their 18th birthday after the date of application but before the date of decision, you must assess the application as if the applicant was still under 18.
proposals.why: exception covers the narrower case where the child turns 18 between application and decision, changing the outcome to treat them as under 18.

proposals.rule: You cannot start or run a business
proposals.exception: You can do a second job in certain circumstances
proposals.why: B narrows the rule to allow a second job under specific circumstances, changing the outcome for that narrower case

proposals.rule: You cannot change employer unless you apply to update your visa.
proposals.exception: If you start a different, eligible job with the same employer you do not need to update your visa.
proposals.why: The exception applies only when the new job is with the same employer and is eligible, allowing no visa update.
